SOURCE: "Autogenesis: A Self-Evolving Agent Protocol", Wentao Zhang, Zhe Zhao, Haibin Wen (equal contribution) et al., Ming Yin and Bo An (corresponding). Preprint, arXiv 2604.15034v6 (8 Oct 2026), marked "Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2027". First submission is April 2026 by the arXiv ID; the PDF is v6. Code: github.com/DVampire/Autogenesis.
COVERAGE: 34 of 34 pages and 117,161 of 117,161 chars read, including the appendices. References were skimmed. Text extraction is clean. Figures were read only from their text labels, with no image rendering.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: AGP separates what evolves (RSPL: Prompt, Agent, Tool, Environment, Memory as versioned, registered resources) from how updates are proposed (SEPL: Reflect, Select, Improve, Evaluate, Commit). The protocol requires that proposal and assessment leave the active resource and its bindings unchanged. Only an accepted commit publishes a new version.
  number: none
  setup: reflection instantiation used in all experiments. Textual-feedback, REINFORCE++-style and GRPO-style adapters are unevaluated sketches.
  quote: "The protocol requires proposal and assessment to leave active resource configurations and bindings unchanged; only accepted commits may publish updates."
  where: Sec 3.2.2, p4
- Claim: Rejection keeps the active version. This is distinct from restoring a retained version, and publishing a version is distinct from binding consumers to it. Publication does not switch in-flight consumers.
  number: none
  setup: design rules. The cases show only accepted updates and never exercise rollback.
  quote: "Commit records an accepted version for subsequent use; publication and consumer binding are distinct events."
  where: p5; also Sec 4 "Publication does not automatically switch every in-flight consumer"
- Claim: Joint prompt and solution evolution raised GPT-4o GPQA-Diamond accuracy over the strongest controls, at about 52-61% more output tokens. The authors say this is a higher-accuracy operating point, not an equal-compute advantage.
  number: GPQA 59.09% (351/594) vs Simple Reflection 54.04% (321/594); AIME24 15/90 vs Best-of-3 13/90; AIME25 12/90 vs Simple Reflection 9/90. Gains are 5.05, 2.22 and 3.33 pp, with about 61%, 57% and 52% more tokens.
  setup: GPT-4o via OpenRouter, temperature 0.7, three runs of the same 198 or 30 questions, at most 3 primary generation opportunities, 32,768 output-token cap per call. Output tokens per problem on GPQA: Vanilla 299, SC 896, Bo3 1,033, SR 1,141, Joint 1,838.
  quote: "Gains are 5.05, 2.22, and 3.33 percentage points, with approximately 61%, 57%, and 52% more output tokens than these respective controls."
  where: Sec 5.1, p7; Tables 4-5, p17
- Claim: The evaluator is a separate call to the same backbone, with no reference labels. It returns a Boolean plus a rationale and checks consistency, completeness and format, not correctness. The authors concede the gate can accept wrong edits.
  number: none
  quote: "A satisfaction gate can be wrong and does not enforce true-performance monotonicity."
  where: Appx G.3.4 (p29); Sec 3 feedback boundaries (p5); Table 6, p18
- Claim: Multi-model reasoning table. Evolution generally helps, but joint editing is not uniformly best.
  number: GPT-4o GPQA 47.98 -> 58.08; GPT-4.1 AIME24 23.33 -> 40.00; Grok-4.1-fast AIME24 96.67 unchanged for all variants; GPT-4.1 GPQA joint 67.68 vs 68.69 for single-target variants.
  setup: single runs, up to 3 reflection rounds, no tools. A 30-question AIME set moves 3.33 pp per answer.
  quote: "Joint editing is therefore not uniformly preferable, and its benefit should be weighed against inference cost."
  where: Table 1 p6; Sec 5.1 p7
- Claim: Agent-Evo (edits to prompts, tools and code) improves GAIA within the AGS system. The largest test gain is at Level 3, with no validation gain there.
  number: validation 89.70 -> 93.33; test 79.07 -> 89.04; L3 test 61.22 -> 81.63; L3 validation 88.46 -> 88.46; HLE 59.6
  setup: gemini-3.1-pro-preview, planner with 30 steps and five specialists with 20 steps each. External leaderboard rows use different backbones and budgets, so they are not a controlled comparison.
  quote: "Agent-Evo increases reported GAIA validation accuracy from 89.70 to 93.33 and test accuracy from 79.07 to 89.04 within the AGS configuration, and AGS scores 59.6 on HLE."
  where: Sec 5.2, p8
- Claim: Execution-feedback revision raised LeetCode solves in all five languages. Mean runtime fell, but memory and percentiles were mixed. The gain bundles revision with extra attempts.
  number: solved counts Python3 79 -> 87, C++ 84 -> 99, Java 84 -> 98, Go 82 -> 95, Kotlin 75 -> 95.
  setup: gemini-3-flash-preview, 100 recent LeetCode problems, initial submission plus up to 2 judge-feedback revisions. Contamination is not ruled out.
  quote: "Solution-Evo increases solved counts from 79 to 87 in Python3, 84 to 99 in C++, 84 to 98 in Java, 82 to 95 in Go, and 75 to 95 in Kotlin."
  where: Sec 5.3, p8; Appx F.2: "rather than an equal-computation advantage"
- Claim: System cost is significant.
  number: about 49 inference steps and 23 min per GAIA task; 67 steps and 11 min per HLE task; 12 steps and 4 min per coding task. Total spend about USD 2,000, 6,000 and 200 respectively.
  setup: aggregate figures, not matched-cost comparisons between variants. GAIA and HLE ran April 2026, coding February 2026.
  quote: "AGS uses approximately 49 model-inference steps and 23 minutes per GAIA task, 67 steps and 11 minutes per HLE task (including judging), and 12 steps and 4 minutes per coding task."
  where: Appx B.1, p18
- Claim: Memory case. A policy edit (tag "verified/constraint" records into a separate store) changed what the memory returns. This is a retrieval result, not an accuracy gain, and may owe part of its effect to extra storage.
  number: verified constraints returned 0/8 -> 8/8; ordinary recent records 25 -> 25; 45 records written (8 constraints + 37 ordinary).
  setup: one GAIA-derived L3 replay, deterministic, candidate version v1.0.4, gemini-3.1-pro-preview.
  quote: "On the same 45-record workload, returned constraints increase from zero to eight, with 25 ordinary recent records preserved."
  where: Sec 5.4 p9; Fig 7 p16
- Claim: Frozen built-ins are not edited. A new resource is registered instead (new Agent beside a frozen built-in; Tool at v1.0.0; Prompt v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0). Candidates are checked on input-derived checks, with no benchmark answer, before commit.
  number: none
  setup: three selected accepted cases (spreadsheet, map Environment, Memory), not population-level evidence.
  quote: "The frozen built-in Agent is not edited: a new Agent supplies the missing aggregation contract."
  where: App A.1, p14

LIMITS
- Authors concede these: "We do not isolate resource management from the update strategy or establish equal-cost superiority, cross-task transfer, or recovery after faulty activation." (p9)
- Version history is not a safety guarantee: "Version histories provide inspection records and restoration targets for retained internal state; they do not guarantee behavioral safety or monotonic improvement." Self-evaluation may accept incorrect changes. External actions may be irreversible. Executable edits need deployment-specific isolation and permissions. Sandboxing of evaluation code is "left to the deployment".
- Restoration assumes mediated mutations and a trusted registry. It covers only captured internal state. It does not rewind episode data or external effects unless those were separately captured. Restoration is "not a system-wide transaction". A version string alone does not ensure an immutable snapshot or a failure-atomic update. An interrupted update must not expose a candidate.
- Evolvability markers restrict edits "through the manager, not operating-system permissions". The flag is not authorization to execute generated code, access files or transmit data.
- The AIME sets have 30 questions. Three runs per method is too few for population claims. The repeated runs share the same questions. Best-of-3 and Simple Reflection are matched on primary opportunities, not on total calls or tokens.
- There was no ablation that holds the editor, feedback and realized budget fixed. The comparison with MCP, A2A and other optimizers (Self-Refine, Reflexion, TextGrad, MIPRO, GEPA, AFlow, EvoAgentX, Alita) is about mechanisms, not matched performance.
- The TextGrad, REINFORCE++ and GRPO adapters have no post-edit acceptance gate and are unvalidated. The GRPO and REINFORCE++ sketches use text similarity, not likelihood ratios.
- The LeetCode-derived content, task traces and platform tools are excluded from the release, so the coding results cannot be independently reproduced. Contamination is not excluded.
- Dated: results use gemini-3.1-pro, gemini-3-flash-preview and GPT-4o. The leaderboard comparisons are a snapshot from 2025 and 2026.

BUILDS ON: ReAct (Yao et al., 2023); AutoGen (Wu et al., 2024); MetaGPT (Hong et al., 2024); AgentVerse (Chen et al., 2024); MCP and A2A specs (2025, 2026); Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023); Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023); TextGrad (Yuksekgonul et al., 2025); MIPRO (Opsahl-Ong et al., 2024); GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2026); AFlow (Zhang et al., 2025b); EvoAgentX (Wang et al., 2025); Alita (Qiu et al., 2025); AgentOrchestra (Zhang et al., 2025c) for the planner-specialist design; Anthropic Agent Skills (2025).

CODE (verbatim)
- Algorithm 1 control flow (p29-30): loop for t=1..T; "if Stop(V,Z,F) break; H<-Reflect(Z,V,F); D<-Select(V,H) {respect evolvability markers}; Ṽ<-ImproveCandidate(V,D); S<-EvaluateCandidate(Ṽ,G); if Accept(S) then V<-Commit(Ṽ,S) else Keep V unchanged; record candidate rejection; F<-AppendAssessment(F,S)". Rejected assessments feed later Reflect calls.
- Commit wrapper (eq 12, p28): the retained state passes through unchanged unless Accept(S).
- Memory policy sketch (p16): markers = ["established","verified","confirmed","constraint","fact"]; if any(k in text for k in markers): state.confirmed_constraints.append(record).
- RSPL record (Def 3.2): c = (entity, version, implementation η, parameters θ, exported representations F). Entity = (name, description, invocation mapping, evolvability marker g in {0,1}, metadata).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p3): architecture, with RSPL, the five-step SEPL loop (Reflect, Select, Improve, Evaluate, Commit), "accept: publish v'; reject: retain v", and the version lineage. Best single picture of the release-process framing.
- Fig 5 (p14): Tool, Agent and Prompt evolution on a spreadsheet task, with a commit after each input-derived check.
- Fig 7 (p16): Memory-policy replay, 0/8 to 8/8 constraints, with the policy sketch.
- Fig 3 (p7): accuracy versus output-token cost across Vanilla, SC, Bo3, SR and Joint. Useful for the cost trade-off.
- Fig 6 (p15): Environment transition-model repair. Notes that episode-local undo is not version rollback.
- Fig 2 (p6): HLE leaderboard. Fig 4 (p9): coding metrics over task count. Not needed for note 08.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found.
- Text extraction is clean, but the figure and table text is jumbled in places. Table 3 gain rows are partly garbled, so I quoted only the solved counts from the prose.
- Table 2 and Fig 2 compare against external systems that are not matched in backbone or budget. Do not cite them as controlled.
- Practical note for the note: this is a protocol or lifecycle paper. Its guardrail value for note 09 is the commit-gated, versioned, rejection-preserving design and the explicit limits. It does not show that rollback works, and its gate is a self-assessed Boolean.
